name: Raised / Elevated Latrine
description: Pit or vault built above ground level (mound or concrete ring riser) with stairs/ramp, preventing surface runoff ingress and keeping the pit bottom safely above high seasonal water tables.
plain_advantages: Elevated above floodwaters; functional in waterlogged or high-water-table areas without water supply.
plain_disadvantages: Requires stairs or ramp (accessibility challenge for elderly or disabled); emptying elevated pits requires manual or vacuum service.

name: Lined / Sealed Pit Latrine with Vent (VIP)
description: Offset or direct pit with reinforced masonry/concrete lining, vent pipe with fly screen, and cover slab. Sealed lower sections protect shallow aquifers from direct horizontal leachate.
plain_advantages: Low cost, easy community maintenance, no water needed, fly and odor reduction via ventilation pipe.
plain_disadvantages: Cannot be used if groundwater is shallower than 1.5m; vulnerable to collapse in unlined sandy soils or flooding if not elevated.

name: Urine-Diverting Dry Toilet (UDDT)
description: Double-vault above-ground system separating urine from feces at the pan. Feces dehydrate with ash/sawdust in sealed chambers; urine is collected separately for agricultural nitrogen fertilization.
plain_advantages: Completely above ground (zero groundwater contamination); requires no water; provides valuable pathogen-free fertilizer.
plain_disadvantages: Requires user education on separation and adding cover material; double chamber rotation requires active user management.

name: Composting Toilet / Arborloo
description: Shallow pit or vault system where carbonaceous organic material (leaves, sawdust, soil) is regularly added to aerate and compost biological solids into humus over 6-12 months.
plain_advantages: Very inexpensive, simple local materials, enriches soil for tree planting and agroforestry.
plain_disadvantages: Requires yard space to rotate or move; vulnerable to flooding if pit is unlined; requires active compost turning and curing.

name: Septic Tank with Soak Pit / Leach Field
description: Water-tight 2-chamber settling and anaerobic digestion tank followed by a gravel-lined soakaway pit for effluent soil percolation. Requires periodic fecal sludge emptying.
plain_advantages: Hygienic flush user experience, high odor containment, long desludging interval if correctly sized.
plain_disadvantages: Fails in impermeable clay soils or shallow water tables (effluent surfaces, contaminating wells); requires steady flush water (>15L/capita/day).

name: Twin-Pit Pour-Flush Latrine
description: Water-seal toilet bowl connected via a diversion junction box to two alternating offset honeycomb-lined pits. One pit fills over 2 years while the resting pit safely decomposes into safe fertilizer.
plain_advantages: Water-seal eliminates insects and odors; only needs 1.5-2L pour water; perpetual cycle with in-situ self-sanitizing pits.
plain_disadvantages: Requires permeable soil for percolation; high water table contaminates groundwater; cannot function during riverine flooding.

name: Container-Based Sanitation (CBS)
description: Portable, sealed cartridge toilets where human excreta is captured in odor-tight removable containers and collected on a weekly logistics schedule for centralized treatment and nutrient/biomass recovery.
plain_advantages: Completely immune to high water tables, rocky terrain, and flooding; zero water needed; compact for dense informal settlements.
plain_disadvantages: Requires reliable ongoing logistics service provider for container collection; ongoing subscription/service fee.

name: Decentralized Wastewater Treatment (DEWATS) & Constructed Wetland
description: Cluster or settlement-scale anaerobic baffled reactors followed by subsurface horizontal/vertical constructed wetland gravel beds planted with emergent macrophytes (reeds, cattails).
plain_advantages: No electricity required (passive gravity biological purification); produces polished effluent safe for community agriculture/irrigation.
plain_disadvantages: Requires dedicated communal land footprint (constructed wetland bed); requires coordinated settlement sewer collection piping.

name: Off-Site Conventional / Simplified Sewer Network
description: Underground gravity or shallow condominial piped sewer network conveying blackwater and greywater directly to a municipal treatment plant or stabilization ponds.
plain_advantages: Complete off-site removal of wastewater; standard urban gold standard; zero local pit emptying needed.
plain_disadvantages: Highest capital cost; vulnerable to chronic blockages if water supply is insufficient (<40L/capita/day); pipes subject to infiltration and backflow during riverine floods.
